activity.overview: Show what you know about alleles, crosses and probability. Draw a Punnett square for every cross.

problems.prompt: Freckles (F) are dominant to no freckles (f). Define genotype, phenotype, homozygous and heterozygous, using this gene for an example of each.
A heterozygous person with freckles has children with a person who has no freckles. What is the probability that a child has no freckles? Show the Punnett square.

Two heterozygous parents have three children, all of whom show the dominant trait. A friend says their fourth child is now certain to show the recessive trait. Is the friend right? Explain using probability.

In pea plants, round seeds (R) are dominant to wrinkled (r), and yellow seeds (Y) are dominant to green (y). The two genes are inherited independently. Cross RrYy x RrYy. Give the phenotype ratio, and calculate the probability of a wrinkled green seed using the multiplication rule.
A child has type O blood. The mother has type A blood. Three men are possible fathers: one has type A, one has type B, and one has type AB. Which man can be ruled out? Explain using genotypes.
Hemophilia is an X-linked recessive condition. Explain why it is much more common in males than in females.

A student crosses two heterozygous plants and counts 200 offspring: 142 show the dominant trait and 58 show the recessive trait. What numbers did the 3:1 model predict? Are the results consistent with the model? Explain.
